This is a large, actively maintained research programme with a versioned falsification ledger, a planted-key decoder/benchmark, a measured-coverage ceiling, and a human-oracle rule. Its current Round45 kickoff and measured-ceiling snapshot report no LP2 solution. Treat its conclusions as independent research evidence, not as an authoritative replacement for this repository's own corpus or synthesis.

## Round 44 findings relevant here

- **T7 — non-stationary anti-repeat slip rate.** Dukotah R44 reports 86 page-local adjacent-equality sites, 13-bin counts `[8,3,7,2,6,9,10,8,11,2,9,6,5]`, gap autocorrelation +0.380, battery p=0.0010 and a gap-permutation tail p=0.00025. njloof campaign #10 independently replicated the gap statistic (p=0.0006 under its hard-core null). This does **not** establish generator memory: the local repository's stronger source-boundary analysis finds the gap signal is largely inherited from the selection of the 85 event-bearing words (word-index gap correlation +0.38545; exact word-identity conditional upper tail p=0.259137). See `im-results/lp2-doublet-block-marginal-control.md` and `im-results/lp2-doublet-gap-source-boundary-conditional-gate.md`. **Correction to njloof #10 wording:** its “1,649-rune doublet-free void” was corrected in campaign #18; the span is sparse, not zero-event. Exact first-rune 1-based sites are 2740, 3140, 3852, 4389 (gaps 400, 712, 537), leaving two internal sites. It lies within decoration group P4; group-containment test p=0.27. Follow-ups report p15-axis alignment p=0.0168, post-hoc p15-grid containment p≈2.6e-4, but the 16-number pointer readout has 0/16 hits (p=1.0). These are structural observations, not plaintext or a key.
- **R1 — page/line/section key resets on the p27/p54 boundary-crossing 7-gram.** The external lane tests 51 fixed source-derived keys, 30 offsets, six configurations, three reset modes, and 55 rune-bearing pages (about 1.5 million cells). It reports zero crossers. Its same-plaintext 7-gram constraint excludes every swept key at offsets up to 200; the different-plaintext interpretation remains open. This is broader than the current repository's simple p27/p55 periodic-key gate and is a useful independent negative. It does not exclude reset mechanisms outside those 51 keys/configurations.
- **p27:93 glyph adjudication.** The external audit resolves the glyph as U, agreeing with the current canon. A competing B label came from one mislabelled singleton exemplar caused by a merged C+B glyph on p13. No canon change was made. This is a useful source-side cross-check, not plaintext recovery.
- **p50 256-byte payload.** The external resolved `canon_256.hex` is byte-for-byte identical across all 256 bytes to this repository's `resources/liber-primus/lp2-grid-256.json`. The current p50 table therefore already contains the external three-byte resolution; no re-transcription is needed.
- **JPEG DQT split.** The two page groups differ by grayscale (one SOF component) versus color/YCbCr (three components), while sharing an identical Annex-K luma table at Q=92. Ink-coverage complexity is indistinguishable (MW p=0.338). The authors classify this as a benign production-pipeline signal with zero ciphertext bearing.

The Round 44 closeout also reports negative results for red-ink, p15 grid, punctuation/quote channels, onion-blob pads, 7-gram cipher readings, chained presentation, hash stride, cuneiform census, all-pairs page-XOR, delta composites (k\ge7), short-page language screens, homophonic screens, and audio reductions. Some overlap current work; check the live ledger before repeating any lane.

## Round 45 closeout — printed separators, order and transcription (24 November 2026)

Pinned upstream HEAD `0335ecf3f0d47c0dc6ecd953bcc729bce6ccad46` adds a material structural result beyond the earlier Round45 kickoff snapshot.

- **W1 — no plaintext word-length order at any tested scope.** On the rune-identical 12,956-rune / 2,896-group LP2 stream, 12 order tests across global, sentence, line, paragraph, page and section scopes are null (all empirical (p\geq0.38)); intact English controls have 100% power. The LP2 length multiset is English-shaped rather than geometric spacing (the cross-corpus multiset test reports (p=0.060)), but the scope of any permutation is not identifiable. Do not turn this into the stronger claim that the spaces are definitely fake or globally shuffled.
- **Q4 — adjacent-equality suppression across printed groups.** The measured boundary rate is 23/2,895 versus 63/10,060 within groups. Upstream estimates q=0.060 and a plug-in upper bound near 0.20 using a common within-group residual rate and 1/29 equality probability for rewired pairs. The bound is conditional on those assumptions; it does not identify a literal rejection filter, key-clock continuity, or directed reading order. Word-local key resets can coexist with a continuous output-layer constraint. Q3 finds no detectable boundary leakage at the tested ≥10% keyed-rewiring level, but is blind under an OTP-class key. [Critic identifiability audit](../../communications/broadcast/2026-11-25T0212Z_critic_q4_boundary_identifiability.md).
- **I1 — keep two distinct space hypotheses.** Under **H-shuffle**, printed groups are genuine word units whose order is permuted; per-group lexical constraints may remain informative, while sequential word-position/grammar claims do not. Under **H-decoy**, groups are not the plaintext's word segmentation; intact-group lexical constraints, word-indexed clocks and word-local resets lose their claimed power. W1 does not distinguish H-shuffle from H-decoy. The ten upstream rows specifically marked conditional on in-order spaces are C-01; R37-C1-U2 (U2b only); R37-C1-U3; R38-C1-SEMANTIC-WORDNET; R38-C1-SEMANTIC-FREQRANK; R39-C1-SENSE-SIMILARITY; R38-C2-G3-LAGGED-POINTERS; R41-C1-R14-WORDSUM-SELFKEY (W1–W4); R44-W2A2-7GRAM-DIFFPLAIN; and R40-C1-INCONCLUSIVE-R31. This is not a blanket invalidation of spacing-free or rune-stream attacks.
- **Human-oracle correction.** Upstream amended `HUMAN-ORACLE.md` §3: word-salad order alone is not grounds to reject a candidate as NOISE-CROSSER; assess word-bag fluency separately from word order.
- **Transcription control.** S1 reports zero canon errors among 398 adjudicated glyphs, including all 86 adjacent-equality sites. The 149 RAT positions previously discussed are unaligned positions, not 149 canon disagreements; no correction to the local canon is proposed.

**Decision:** this is an external, independently reproducible structural constraint, not a plaintext or key. For local work, retain every result's declared segmentation assumption: group-based negatives are conditional on H-shuffle; under H-decoy they must not be promoted to all-segmentation exclusions. Do not repeat generic word-length MI or infer a source-selected word permutation from the length multiset alone.

## Current word/meaning/number clue ceiling — 25 November 2026

Pinned upstream HEAD `593247d84689531432ec642b0f57d1e487bb28c9` updates `liber-primus/MEASURED-CEILING.md`. For the signed 2016 instruction, keep these distinct campaigns separate:

- **R9-DIRECTION:** 2,670 reads. The current measured ceiling classifies the post-R40 re-score as **inconclusive**, not a confirmed kill: the best 400-rune stream has pmax 4.733; global doublet-matched shuffle nulls give p=0.004–0.0066, but page-scale and region-scale block-permuted nulls give p=0.018 and 0.070, and the best of 923 trajectories is an ordinary extreme. No readable plaintext was recovered. `research/DEAD_ENDS.md` still retains an older Gate#2 **KILLED** label; this conflicts with the current ceiling and must not be repeated as the current classification without reconciliation.
- **Round10 L2-MAP:** the preregistered cleartext printed-word channel covers 77,672 primary readings across M1–M9 (word-initial/final streams, word numbers, boundary bits, LP1 dictionary pointers, word walks, structural counts, transposition, LP1 skeleton and direct addressing). The current measured ceiling reports no hit. M9 alone covers 52,164 direct-address tests with no hit; M4's best LP1 lookup is null-matched (z=0.59); M7's word-level transposition is analytically excluded by IoC×N=0.9999 < 1.10; M8's longest LP1-skeleton run is 7 versus null maximum 8. The G1 line-initial anomaly (p=4.1×10⁻⁷) is a typesetting artifact: line-width regression r=0.7233, p=9.29×10⁻⁶, while the D3 line-initial stream has z=3.84, below the preregistered +5 gate. The L2 preregistration's P0 offers a plausible alternative reading: the signed 2016 wording may echo LP1's A WARNING line “either the words or their numbers, for all is sacred,” as devotional restatement rather than a new operational instruction. This is a hypothesis, not an established authorial intent. The L2 tests assume the printed word-boundary channel is cleartext; they do not test semantic content of recovered plaintext.
- **Round10 L3-ROAD:** its preregistered T1a/T1b and T2–T5 family tests ciphertext-word GP sums as reductions, selectors, orderings and keytext pointers over the 2,928-word / 12,956-rune / 55-segment corpus. The current combined R10/R11 ceiling reports 208 road streams and classifies the lane as measured negative, with its direct and beam plants recovered. This tests numbers derived from ciphertext words; it does **not** test semantic meanings of recovered plaintext.
- **R37 C1-U3 composed map/road/direction:** 4,176 decodes on page heads 0–2; best score 4.484 against a 6.632 bar, classified measured negative.
- **R38/R39 semantic-address and sense-position:** 28,224 and 14,112 readings are classified negative. The same current ceiling says 18 F5 semantic cells beyond one generic operationalization remain partial. The semantic-content reading of “meaning is the road” is therefore not falsified; it needs recovered plaintext or a source-specified semantic resource and indexing rule. Do not substitute arbitrary dictionary/WordNet sweeps.

The external campaigns do not test this repository's separate p15 geometry-key candidate. Local p15 receiver and holdout evidence is in [the geometry-key report](../../im-results/lp2-p15-words-geometry-key.md).

## Distinct primary-artifact cross-checks (15 November audit)

- **Three authentic signed January 2014 hexadecimal blocks, identified as the known three OutGuess shares.** The clear-signed hex bodies of `2014-01-liber-primus-hash-block.asc`, `2014-01-liber-primus-hash-block-outguess-01.asc`, and `2014-01-liber-primus-hash-block-outguess-02.asc` are **byte-for-byte identical, in that order**, to `sources[0..2].hex` in our pre-existing `resources/cicada2014-outguess-hex.json`. Their positionwise XOR yields **exactly** the 991 bytes of upstream `2014-01-signed-ciphertext.asc`, including its signed 70-character transposition clue and OpenPGP signature. This is the already solved *January 2014 OutGuess-share stage*, not a second independent triple or an untested joint cipher (§ [historical reconstruction](../../workplace/historical-solve-path-to-original-lp2.md), closed [#263](https://github.com/FlareZ123/liber-primus/issues/263) and [#327](https://github.com/FlareZ123/liber-primus/issues/327)). The signed message directs players to the contemporaneous next-onion waypoint, without specifying an LP2 key, chapter or receiver. The external Round 44 [B1 original-byte study](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/liber-primus/analysis/round44/W2-B1-hash-stride/RESULTS.md) identifies *three separate* 991-byte binary blocks under 7A35090F-signed .asc messages, with SHA-256 values `f8fa59ec133168d8aaf9c67d13152286eebcec191c5668f7f143a2c7764fc530`, `6600c94b199f30c70c58f5800ccf80537b335122bd66768b6049241d8b20f318`, and `07d660d76e24dac92dc0350881ed7771263905a4a64f66c68f7f88ef77c9e07d`. Their signed armors are retained in the upstream [primary artifact tree](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/tree/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/corpus/A-primary-artifacts/pgp/messages). A preregistered scan of 11,508 windows for MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 digests of 354 extant source representations gave zero matches with two planted hits recovered. This **does not** rule out a hash oracle for as-yet-unrecovered plaintext. The observed `Hash: SHA1` armor line specifies the *PGP signature's digest algorithm*; it does not authenticate a SHA-1 list inside the hex body. No original page decodes or key can currently be claimed from these blocks. If genuine unknown plaintext is independently recovered, the three byte-pinned blocks give a pre-existing, fixed comparison object; avoid repeating the already-exhausted existing-ciphertext digest grid.
- **The Round 43 original onion-2 timing lane has been superseded locally on coverage.** Upstream [F5b-T](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/liber-primus/analysis/round43/F5bT-timing-keystream/RESULTS.md) merged 112 exact five-minute-multiple intervals at byte positions 143–256, leaving positions 190–191 bounded. Here `im-results/lp2-2014-onion2-timing-merged-114.json` and `im-results/onion2-five-minute-clock-inference.md` resolve **114/114** corresponding intervals using additional dated source evidence. The local original timing/byte key and two time-interleaving inverses have also produced scoped negatives; the external 112-event beam need not be copied or rerun. For a future timing operation, use the 114-event local evidence, remembering that no authored LP2 clock rule has been identified.
- **Cross-project numbering and red-channel compatibility.** Upstream's “55 unsolved canon pages” means 55 *rune-bearing* encrypted segments: the physical LP2 corpus has 56 unsolved pages p0–p55 because p50 contains only the 256-cell table. Its “canon p55 AN END” is our **physical p56** solved page. [Round 44 red-ink P1](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/blob/9087dc36b5aa64c1786428e32180261ab9420c29/liber-primus/analysis/round44/P1-red-ink/RESULTS.md) expands the old 187-rune red selection to **213 on the 13 unknown red-bearing pages** by including drop-caps, overlooked title and terminal red lines; our `im-results/lp2-red-ink-channel-audit.md` independently already recognizes the same 213 red runes and 30 red 13-/10-dot markings. These counts are compatible, with image indexing requiring the one-page offset. This closes a potential false “new red text” claim.

**Decision:** These are useful source and coverage reconciliations. The audited upstream material supplies no newly authenticated unknown-page plaintext, source-selected invertible key, or untested original-byte operation with an independently frozen ciphertext prediction. Reuse its exact signed blocks as a future keyed/plaintext validation object and pursue independent original-source selector discovery; there is no basis for a new broad enumeration.

- [`af0cc45`](https://github.com/2retooz270703/Liber-Primus-27x27-Map-3-Rune-Nodes-Totient-Decryption/commit/af0cc451933d344c1e7ed13843740c6bdd07b302) (16:08:30Z): adds the `DIE`/5,360 GP-sum correspondence.

- [`c2dea44`](https://github.com/2retooz270703/Liber-Primus-27x27-Map-3-Rune-Nodes-Totient-Decryption/commit/c2dea442f6537c9357aaafcfef9c9930bf870afa) (16:17:29Z): changes “proposed main route” to “main route.”

**Independent arithmetic check against the local original-corpus file** [`lp2-corpus.json`](../liber-primus/lp2-corpus.json):
- p0–p2 contain 262 + 266 + 201 = **729** runes.
- Claimed source cells (18,10), (18,14), (18,18) contain indices [5,23,27] = C/K–D–IA. Their `μ(φ(index))) signature is [0,+1,0], giving phase 1 and aligned key [23,27,5] = D–IA–C/K.
- Claimed ciphertext cells (3,22), (4,23), (5,24) contain [17,8,23] = B–H–D. Subtraction mod 29 yields [23,10,18] = D–I–E; adding the same key forward reproduces [17,8,23] exactly. The GP sum of DIE is 89+31+67 = **187**.

This confirms one **three-rune arithmetic inverse** on original corpus values. It does not authenticate the selection of the source node, the diagonal ciphertext segment, the key rule, or the endpoint. The candidate is selected from scattered cells of a 729-cell square; it is not a complete contiguous page or a full-page plaintext. The local frozen-geometry report already reproduces the same opening two blocks (12 runes) and shows that the simplest unchanged endpoint-node/rightward-totient continuation fails on its untouched third block; see [the local holdout](../../im-results/lp2-2026-square27-frozen-geometric-plaintext-holdout.md). The new longer route changes the transition family rather than supplying a blind confirmation of that frozen rule.

**Decisive source-selection problem:** the public README's own “Let me explain” section says the branch was found by computer brute-force search and that the author does not know whether it is genuine; the method section says exact next-location selection remains open. Report 24 explicitly says its filter was selected retrospectively: it searched 8,610 input predicates and 4,746 output predicates, chose the output predicate with the full route available, and reports 8/12,000 controls for the fixed selected output versus 1,953/12,000 across 4,071 output predicates. Those are measurements of a post-selected search family, not a prospective source-derived selector. The detailed [DIE walkthrough](https://github.com/2retooz270703/Liber-Primus-27x27-Map-3-Rune-Nodes-Totient-Decryption/blob/main/plaintext-i-found/39-DIE.md) itself calls DIE a candidate and says the transition rules do not independently establish where the message ends. The 5,360 equality is a checksum noticed after the candidate word was known; deleting that caveat in a later commit does not make it prospective.

**Decision:** retain this as an interesting, exactly reproducible local three-rune construction and a public hypothesis about the 27×27 opening. Do **not** promote the 118-rune route, `DIE` endpoint, or GP checksum to recovered plaintext, authentic key material, or a Cicada-selected mechanism. A promotion would require an original clue that fixes the node/receiver/transition family before plaintext inspection and an untouched prospective continuation.

## Measured ceiling and remaining gaps

This section is refreshed against upstream HEAD [`593247d84689531432ec642b0f57d1e487bb28c9`](https://github.com/Dukotah/cicada3301/commit/593247d84689531432ec642b0f57d1e487bb28c9) (Round46). The ceiling is finite and family-scoped; negative results do not prove every interpretation of the signed 2016 statement impossible.

- **R9-DIRECTION:** 2,670 readings across four families. `research/DEAD_ENDS.md` labels the lane refuted, while `MEASURED-CEILING.md` classifies the post-R40 re-score as inconclusive after page-scale and region-scale nulls (p=0.018 and 0.070). Preserve this upstream classification conflict; no plaintext was recovered.
- **R10 L2-MAP:** 77,672 preregistered primary readings across M1–M9; no hit. M9 direct addressing, M4 LP1 dictionary lookup, M7 word-level transposition, and M8 LP1 skeleton all fail their registered gates. The G1 line-initial anomaly is explained by typesetting width, not a word-map signal.
- **R10 L3-ROAD:** 208 road streams plus the registered booklike T5 family; no hit. T1 is control-limited (Paradise Lost has the same two-rune deficit); T2/T3/T4 fail, and the best T5 source is below its signal threshold. These tests concern ciphertext-word sums and selectors, not semantic content of recovered plaintext.
- **R37-C1-U3 composed map/road/direction:** 4,176 decodes; measured negative.
- **R38 semantic-address (28,224) and R39 sense-position (14,112):** measured negative under the tested operationalizations. The upstream handoff still leaves semantic cells partial; the semantic-content reading requires recovered plaintext or a source-specified semantic resource and indexing rule. Do not substitute arbitrary WordNet/dictionary sweeps.
- **Round46 structural update:** corrected 2,896-word/420-wrap loader; R41-C1-R14 negative at full power; C-01 SKELETON at chance/conditional; R37-U2b/U3 and R44-7GRAM hold; R38-C2-G3 not rerun; two-rune deficit is register-dependent; line-break lead descriptive only. No key-space sweep and no LP2 plaintext/key.
- The signed 2016 line remains authentic first-party language, but the external P0 reading that it echoes LP1 A WARNING as devotional restatement is plausible, not established. The cleartext word-map and ciphertext-word-number readings have been extensively tested; the semantic meaning of a future decrypted text remains open.

Use the latest handoff and live ledger for any newer work. The upstream scope is not a global proof of impossibility.

## Recommended use

- Do not repeat the T7 block-count or gap-autocorrelation tests, or treat the 1,649 span as a zero-event void. The local word-identity conditional gate explains most of the gap correlation; a new T7 task would need to predict the identities of event-bearing words or a source-selected reversible encoder, not merely remeasure the span. Also do not repeat the p27/p54 51-key reset family or p50/p27:93 source adjudications.
- Do not repeat R9-DIRECTION or R37–R39 numeric/position/length/semantic-position sweeps.
- Reopen the signed 2016 map/road/direction clue only when an original source supplies a determinate semantic per-word index or an independently supported LP1 codebook order.
- Treat remaining measured-ceiling gaps as a coverage map, not a task list. Select work only where an original clue supplies the missing key, operation, or discriminating prediction.
